proposed_english: the prochos / the projection / the cosmic mirror-vault
rationale: Recurring technical term on this page (lines 10, 17, 24, 30, 31) for a cosmological structure that (a) stands before the Great Gate of Honor, (b) contains and displays the twelve seals, the archons, all firmaments, spheres, stars, and powers, (c) is the means by which archonic intentions are 'made manifest forth,' and (d) is explicitly likened to 'a great mirror' (ⲟⲩⲛⲁϭ ⲛ̄ⲓ̈ⲉⲗ) and is 'this judgment of all the works.' Etymology uncertain: possibly Greek πρόχοος ('pitcher, outpouring'), προχοή ('outflow'), πρόοχος ('jutting forth'), or even τρόχος ('wheel') with dialectal substitution. The cosmic-mirror function is well-attested in Manichaean cosmology (the cosmic wheel/mirror revealing all things). Recommend transliterating until parallels in subsequent pages clarify.
ⲡⲁⲛ- (Greek παν- 'all') + ϭⲁⲙ ('power'). Hybrid Greek-Coptic compound 'the all-power(s)' = totality of cosmic powers, paired with spheres and stars in line 11.
Lycopolitan ⲧⲁⲃⲉϩ = Sahidic ⲧⲱⲃⲉ 'seal, signet.' The Twelve Seals of the prochos correspond to the twelve cosmic divisions/zodiacal seals that govern the firmaments.

Greek ἀρχιφύλαξ — 'chief-guardian.' Manichaean cosmological figure standing at the Great Gate of Honor, before whom the prochos stretches like a chain. Distinct from the more general ⲡⲉⲣⲥⲓⲥ guards in earlier vocab.
Lycopolitan ⲓ̈ⲉⲗ = Sahidic ⲉⲓⲁⲗ 'mirror, glass.' The prochos is identified as 'a great mirror' (ⲟⲩⲛⲁϭ ⲛ̄ⲓ̈ⲉⲗ) — a Manichaean cosmological term for the reflective cosmic structure.
Lycopolitan ⲕⲣⲁϩ = Sahidic ⲕⲣⲟϥ 'deceit, guile, treachery.' Stock Coptic moral-vocabulary term.

ⲛⲁϭ ('great') + ⲡⲣⲟ ('gate') + ⲧⲁⲓ̈ⲟ ('honor'). Manichaean cosmological term for the supreme threshold — likely Greek πύλη μεγάλη τῆς δόξης. The whole 'purpose of heart' of this Gate is invested in the prochos that stands before it. Recurs three times on this page (lines 2, 13, 20-21) and structures the whole chapter.
